title: Exceptional adjoint of extension by zero
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and finite coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$, and all operations are the specified derived operations on $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ with exceptional adjunctions [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $f,t:P\to X$ be $k$-morphisms, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], $V=t^{-1}(U)$ and $e:V\hookrightarrow P$ its inclusion. Assume $fe=jh$ for a morphism $h:V\to U$, and put $r=t|_V:V\to U$. For $L\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ and $z:r^*L\to h^!L$, let $w:Rh_!r^*L\to L$ be its exceptional adjoint. Define the open extension $z_X:t^*j_!L\to f^!j_!L$ by
$$t^*j_!L\simeq e_!r^*L\xrightarrow{e_!z}e_!h^!L\longrightarrow f^!j_!L,$$
where the last arrow is the exceptional transpose of
$$Rf_!e_!h^!L\simeq j_!Rh_!h^!L\xrightarrow{j_!\varepsilon_h}j_!L.$$
Under the canonical open base-change and compact-support composition identification
$$Rf_!t^*j_!L\simeq j_!Rh_!r^*L,$$
the exceptional adjoint of $z_X$ is $j_!w$.
Moreover, for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:t^*K\to f^!K$ with adjoint $v:Rf_!t^*K\to K$, take $L=j^*K$ and let $u|_V:r^*L\to h^!L$ be the open restriction, formed using $e^*f^!K\simeq h^!j^*K$. If $a:j_!j^*K\to K$ is the open counit, the preceding adjoint obeys
$$a\circ j_!w=v\circ Rf_!t^*(a),$$
with the same canonical source identification.

source.place: §1.1.6(a)(i), §1.1.8(ii), §1.1.9 and §1.5.9; §5.3.3, open graded identification; legs interchanged

proof.text: Write $F=Rf_!$, $H=Rh_!$, $E=e_!$ and $J=j_!$. For the open immersions $e$ and $j$, the factorizations $(e,\mathrm{id}_P)$ and $(j,\mathrm{id}_X)$ are compactifications, and the identity being proper, the compact-support direct image of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] computed with them is $Re_!=R(\mathrm{id}_P)_*e_!=e_!$ and likewise $Rj_!=j_!$; this is the identification of extension by zero with compact-support direct image used throughout. Since $V=t^{-1}(U)$, the square with arrows $(e,r,t,j)$ is Cartesian. Apply [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] to get the specified natural isomorphism $b_L:t^*JL\xrightarrow{\sim}Er^*L$, whose restriction to $V$ is the identity under the open-unit identifications. Compact-support composition in [prop-functor-package], applied to $fe=jh$, gives a natural isomorphism $C_N:FEN\xrightarrow{\sim}JHN$. The source identification in the statement is therefore $C_{r^*L}\circ F(b_L)$. All these functors are on the finite-coefficient constructible finite-Tor domains specified in [def-trf-admissibility]; no integral or rational coefficient passage is involved.

source.place: §1.1.6(a)(i), §1.5.9: Cartesian source-leg square and compact-support composition; legs interchanged

proof.text:
Let $d_L:Eh^!L\to f^!JL$ be the last arrow defining $z_X$. Write $\varepsilon_f$ and $\varepsilon_h$ for the exceptional counits of [def-trf-admissibility]. The definition of $d_L$ says
$$\varepsilon_{f,JL}\circ F(d_L)=J(\varepsilon_{h,L})\circ C_{h^!L}.$$
Consequently the exceptional transpose of $z_X=d_L\circ E(z)\circ b_L$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{f,JL}\circ F(z_X)
&=J(\varepsilon_{h,L})\circ C_{h^!L}\circ FE(z)\circ F(b_L)\\
&=J(\varepsilon_{h,L}\circ H(z))\circ C_{r^*L}\circ F(b_L).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is naturality of $C$. Since $w=\varepsilon_{h,L}\circ H(z)$ by the same adjunction, this proves the first assertion with exactly the source identification of step 1.

source.place: §1.1.6(a), pushforward formula, rewritten through the exceptional adjunction

proof.text:
For the second assertion denote the open counits by $c_e:Ee^*\to\mathrm{id}$ and $c_j:Jj^*\to\mathrm{id}$. Their adjunctions and invertible units are [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], applied to $e$ and $j$ with their closed complements. For $N\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the two composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(FEN,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,e^*f^!K),\qquad
\operatorname{Hom}(JHN,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,h^!j^*K).$$
Thus the inverse conjugate of $C:FE\simeq JH$ is the canonical $\chi_K:e^*f^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}h^!j^*K$. This is the composition normalization stipulated in [def-trf-admissibility], using $e^!=e^*$ and $j^!=j^*$ as right adjoints of extension by zero. Expanding conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and the composite counits gives
$$\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(c_{e,f^!K})
=c_{j,K}\circ J(\varepsilon_{h,j^*K})\circ JH(\chi_K)\circ C_{e^*f^!K}.\tag{*}$$
Indeed the left side is the counit of $FE\dashv e^*f^!$; the first two arrows on the right are the counit of $JH\dashv h^!j^*$, and inserting the defining unit--transformation--counit formula for the conjugate cancels its adjacent unit and counit by a triangle identity. This also shows why only $fe=jh$, not a Cartesian square for $f$, is needed here.

source.place: §1.1.8(ii) and §1.1.9, open restriction via the two composite adjunctions

proof.text:
Put $L=j^*K$, $Q=t^*K$, and identify $N=r^*L=e^*Q$ by pullback composition. Set $a=c_{j,K}$. Under $b_L$ the pullback of the open counit is the open counit on $P$:
$$t^*(a)\circ b_L^{-1}=c_{e,Q}:EN\longrightarrow Q.\tag{**}$$
To check this, transpose both arrows under $E\dashv e^*$. The transpose of the right side is $\mathrm{id}_{e^*Q}$. For the left side, the restriction-identity normalization of $b_L$ in [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] identifies its transpose with the pullback by $r$ of $j^*(c_{j,K})\circ\eta_{j,j^*K}=\mathrm{id}_{j^*K}$, which is the triangle identity for the open adjunction in [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. The two transposes agree, proving (**).

source.place: §1.1.6(a)(i) and §1.1.8(ii): open base change normalized by the open adjunction

proof.text:
The restricted coefficient is $z=\chi_K\circ e^*(u):N\to h^!j^*K$, so its exceptional transpose is $w=\varepsilon_{h,L}\circ H(z)$. The original transpose is $v=\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(u)$, by [def-trf-admissibility]. Using (**), naturality of $c_e$, then (*) and naturality of $C$, compute
$$\begin{aligned}
v\circ F(t^*a)\circ F(b_L^{-1})
&=\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(u)\circ F(c_{e,Q})\\
&=\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(c_{e,f^!K})\circ FE(e^*u)\\
&=a\circ J(\varepsilon_{h,L})\circ JH(\chi_K)\circ C_{e^*f^!K}\circ FE(e^*u)\\
&=a\circ J(\varepsilon_{h,L}\circ H(z))\circ C_N
=a\circ J(w)\circ C_N.
\end{aligned}$$
The open-counit naturality used here is part of the adjunction of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Composing on the right with $F(b_L)$ proves $v\circ Rf_!t^*(a)=a\circ j_!w$ under $C_N\circ F(b_L)$, exactly as asserted. The computation never uses invertibility of $u$ or $z$.

source.place: §1.5.9 and §5.3.3, open graded coefficient is characterized by compatibility with the open counit; explicit adjunction calculation

proof_origin.place: Explicit adjunction proof of the formulas of §§1.1.6(a)(i), 1.1.8(ii), 1.1.9 and 1.5.9 used in §5.3.3; legs interchanged

split_report.summary: Preserved the exact statement and all inherited records. Gave five explicit steps: normalized open base change and composition; the transpose of the defined extension; the composite-counit formula for arbitrary commuting open squares; pullback compatibility with the open counit; and the final naturality calculation. Reused six existing nodes and created none. Avoided the stronger ambient-adjoint hypothesis of fix-prop-adjunctions by using the specified constructible adjunction datum and the two ordinary open adjunctions.
split_report.blueprint: lem-trf-trace-triangle-compatibility, Induced morphisms paragraph: steps 1–2 realize the three arrows in the extension-by-zero construction; steps 3–5 justify its open restriction and first triangle square, the open coefficient compatibility consumed by the graded identification in Varshavsky §5.3.3.

tool_uses.why: Only compact-support composition for fe=jh is used; the trace-additivity unit has no generic composition theorem.
Open adjunctions, invertible open units and counit naturality normalize the restriction calculation; these are generic recollement tools.
The canonical open base-change isomorphism with restriction equal to the identity supplies the source comparison; it is a tool, not an alternate trace-additivity route.
